source: Muse recheck of first-pass flags; apply through the belt (02 fact block -> 16 -> 04/05 remint), never in place

corrections.corrected_statement: A golf cart may also be driven by day within four miles of a gated community's gate, but only on secondary streets and highways posted at 35 mph or less, under SC Code §56-2-105.
The gate of a gated community can also serve as the starting point for the four-mile daytime golf cart limit.

A South Carolina licensed eye care professional must submit the vision certificate electronically through the online portal while an out of state professional must complete SCDMV Form four one two N C.
corrections.note: Removed on paper because the page does not state a paper filing method.

corrections.corrected_statement: Speed limit signs are black and white signs that indicate the maximum legal speed allowed in ideal conditions.
corrections.note: Removed unsupported claim that posted speed is not guaranteed safe.

corrections.corrected_statement: Guide signs are square or rectangular green brown or blue signs that give information on intersecting roads and help direct you to cities and towns.
corrections.note: Removed unsupported contrast with laws to obey not on cited page.

corrections.corrected_statement: A fluorescent or reflective orange and red triangle on the back of a farm, construction or animal-drawn vehicle means it travels at less than 25 mph, so approach with care and pass only when it is safe.
corrections.note: Triangle identifier text is on page 123, not page 124.

corrections.corrected_statement: For a moving emergency vehicle with lights and siren on, you pull over to the road's edge, which differs from the lane change or slowdown used for a stopped one.
corrections.note: Stopped-vehicle lane-change rule is on page 123, not page 120.

corrections.corrected_statement: Three-point step two: signal left, check traffic and your left blind spot over your shoulder, then turn hard left across the road and stop when you reach the other side.
corrections.note: The completion of step two is printed on page 78, not fully on cited page 77.

corrections.corrected_statement: On a two-lane road you are required to stop for a stopped school bus, whether you are meeting it or following it.
corrections.note: The meeting-or-behind condition is printed on page 82, not on cited page 83.

corrections.corrected_statement: Class E and Class F holders, like Class D holders, may also operate a moped or a three-wheel vehicle, but not a two-wheel motorcycle with a detachable sidecar.

Conditional and special restricted licensees may carry at most two passengers under 21 unless a licensed adult aged 21 or older rides along, except when carrying family members or students to and from school.

Class D allows you to drive noncommercial passenger vehicles such as cars and trucks that do not exceed twenty six thousand pounds gross vehicle weight, and the gross vehicle weight rating or gross vehicle weight determines which class of license you need.
corrections.note: Removed vehicle look language not stated on the page.

corrections.corrected_statement: The final approved supervisor is a responsible adult willing to assume the obligation under South Carolina Code fifty six one one hundred ten who has written permission from any person listed in items one through six signed and verified before a person authorized to administer oaths with a copy provided to the motor vehicle department.
corrections.note: Broadened permission source from parent guardian or custodian to any person in items one through six.

corrections.corrected_statement: Push/pull is the preferred steering method, and the 2 and 10 o'clock hand position is not recommended because it can be dangerous in vehicles with air bags.
corrections.note: Preferred-method language is on page 55, not page 56.

corrections.corrected_statement: Hand-over-hand steering is for low-speed turns such as at intersections or when parking, while push/pull is the preferred method for normal driving.
corrections.note: Preferred-method language is on page 55, not page 56.

corrections.corrected_statement: If a trailer starts to sway or whip, steer straight and slow down gradually without braking, never speed up, and stop once you can get completely off the road.
